rows.description: A bride's family is told there is no demand, just custom, yet lists of items, cash or a lavish wedding are expected. Recognising this as dowry, which is illegal in India, is the first step to refusing it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A bride's parents borrow heavily to meet demands out of fear that their daughter will be mistreated or unmarried. Fear and love push them into harmful custom, and social change needs many families to say no.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A wife faces repeated demands for money or goods after the wedding, or taunts about what her family gave. This is harassment, not custom, and she deserves help from trusted people and legal support.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A friend or neighbour sees a woman withdrawn, watched or blamed about money from her family, and worries. Listening without judgement, keeping contact and pointing to helplines or family support can matter greatly.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A relative who objects to dowry or gender pressure says so calmly at the planning stage and finds allies among elders. Change is often slower than anger, but one clear voice makes others braver.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A parent sees a boy wanting a doll or a girl wanting a bat and decides how to react. A calm response lets the child play; ridicule teaches early that some interests are shameful.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: shame, interest, calm

rows.description: A girl is asked to help in the kitchen while her brother plays, and notices without words. Children learn fairness or unfairness from who does what long before they can name it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenage girl must be home by dark while her brother comes and goes freely, told it is for her safety. She feels both protected and distrusted; open talk about real risks and fair rules helps.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A boy is told to be strong and stop crying, and learns to hide sadness behind jokes or anger. Emotional honesty in boys is a skill that adults need to protect, not mock.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young woman is told to choose an easy job for marriage while a young man is told to earn well. Both are fitted into moulds; real choice comes when each can decide with family support.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
